q: What will SIDBI refuse to finance under its exclusion list?
title: What SIDBI will not finance
short: SIDBI's exclusion list rules out illegal products, weapons, tobacco, spirits other than beer and wine, gambling, asbestos fibres, ozone-depleting substances, banned pesticides, child or forced labour, and coal mining or coal-fired power. It also excludes trading, storing or moving significant volumes of hazardous chemicals, or using them at commercial scale, and counts petrol and kerosene as hazardous.
audience: MSMEs checking whether their business or project can get SIDBI finance

ul: Anything illegal under Indian law or international conventions; weapons and munitions.
Alcoholic beverages other than beer and wine; tobacco; gambling and casinos.
Wildlife trade regulated under CITES; radioactive materials; unbonded asbestos fibres; products containing PCBs.
Pharmaceuticals, pesticides and ozone-depleting substances subject to international phase-outs or bans; persistent organic pollutants.

Production, trade, storage or transport of significant volumes of hazardous chemicals, or their commercial scale use. The list names gasoline, kerosene and other petroleum products as hazardous chemicals.
Prospecting, exploring or mining coal, transport infrastructure essentially used for coal, and power or heating plants essentially fired with coal.
Oil from shale, tar sands or oil sands.
Nuclear power plants, apart from measures that reduce hazards at existing assets.
Logging in primary tropical moist forest, and wood not from sustainably managed forests.
Waste trade across borders unless it complies with the Basel Convention.
Harmful or exploitative child labour, forced labour, and blocking workers from lawful association and collective bargaining.
Projects needing land acquisition or causing displacement or loss of livelihoods.
Projects affecting tribal or indigenous peoples without their documented consent.
Projects in sensitive ecological areas or heritage sites; within 1 km of such an area, the required permissions must be obtained first.

p: The list is SIDBI's organisation-wide exclusion list, reproduced in its environmental and social system for the GCF-backed FMAP programme. The hazardous chemicals line does not define significant volumes or commercial scale, so a fuel trading or storage business, or a plant burning large amounts of furnace oil or diesel, should ask SIDBI how it applies before preparing a full application.

senseible: Senseible does not screen businesses for lender exclusions. It records the fuel and electricity a unit uses, which shows what a fuel-switch or efficiency project would change.
